$comment: What each seat may touch, written once. Setup (plugin screen or install.sh) builds the seats' Paseo providers from the paseo part and copies the file to ~/.config/seatwork/policy.json, where the plugin reads the harness part to build runtimes.

claude.$comment: Claude Code's permission syntax. A tool sits in one named set; a role is denied the sets it lists, in that order. paseoShell: Paseo from the shell; HQ and the Supervisor may read and lose only the commands that act (paseoShellActs). ownOrchestration: Claude's own scheduling, messaging, teams and task list. ownDialogs: what Claude Code opens toward its own user or keeps for itself; behind its question dialog a seat stays in its turn and the room hears nothing, so a seat asks in its final message or by mail. edits: a Lens reads and runs, never writes.
claude.$comment_launch: How a seat starts. Claude seats run on the user's ~/.claude: extraArgs keep the sign-in only (no user settings, no personal MCP server) and env turns off what Claude Code adds itself; strict-mcp-config alone still loads claude.ai connectors. Paseo's own settings flag (fastMode) replaces any other, so the Co-Authored-By reminder is called off in room/harness/claude-system.md instead. Other harnesses get a home of their own: {runtime} is ~/.config/seatwork/runtimes/<harness>/<role>. Setup writes each launch block into the harness's providers (env; extraArgs under options), so a seat starts this way with the plugin off too.
claude.$comment_shareFiles: Files of ~/.claude appended to a Claude seat's prompt; its personal settings are off.
claude.$comment_deniedSkills: Bundled Claude Code skills that overlap the room, denied as Skill(skill:<name>) in the provider's disallowedTools: the guard for a Claude Code that does not know CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS.

runtime.$comment_featuresOff: plugins: left on, Codex syncs its marketplace into every seat's home at each start, and a seat gets no plugin. An owner who sets sharePlugins removes it from this list.

runtime.$comment: A Pi seat gets the room's and Paseo's tools through Pi's built-in MCP (Pi 0.99+), where Paseo registers its servers. settings overlays the user's settings.json: no user package or extension reaches the seat or stands in for that MCP.

daemon.$comment: Daemon-wide switches applied at setup; they reach every agent on the host, not only seats. The setup screen sets browserTools, enableTerminalAgentHooks and bundledSkills and only reports dictation and voiceMode; install.sh sets all five.

mail.$comment: The room's MCP server (seatwork_mail, seatwork_inbox) and delivery rules. Seats never use send_agent_prompt; the plugin delivers each mail whole and interrupts only for a STOP order. A CANDIDATE, REVIEW or DONE to a parent waits for the sender's turn end and is its one report. Starting no turn, read with the next mail: an ACK; a DONE repeated after mail that asked nothing; a Lead's STATUS after its first (only the newest waits); a HOLD or NOTED asking nothing of a Peer under review; the bounce of a mail that asked nothing. gatherReviews: the read-only seats one Owner turn launches (Lens, review and research Peers, scouts) are one round: their REVIEWs wait for the last one, or room.params.reviewStallMinutes, and reach the Owner in one turn.
mail.$comment_midTurn: Mail to a running seat. hold: delivered when its turn ends. steer: Paseo's steer, under which Claude cancels its running tool and Pi aborts it. Keep hold until a harness is seen to apply steer after the tool call.

owner.$comment: chime: while the Paseo app is open, a short sound when a seat nobody above reads by mail (HQ, a Supervisor, a seat you opened yourself) ends a turn with DECISION_NEEDED, BLOCKED, a WAITING ON YOU row or a failure.

gc.$comment: Room garbage collection, every everyMinutes and on agent.archived. A seat idle past its role's hours (0 = never) is archived unless a descendant is alive; a heartbeat of a seat archived or gone is deleted; mail held for an archived seat bounces to its sender. It kills no process and touches no agent that is not a room seat.
gc.$comment_runtimes: What an agent CLI leaves in a seat's home (runtimes/<harness>/<role>) and GC clears, only while none of its seats is open: a running CLI loses nothing and an open seat can still be resumed. rebuilt: entries the CLI makes again (temporary folders, log database), deleted whole. sessions: folders of session records; a file goes once unwritten for keepLogDays (shared/settings.json), with the transcript of its archived seat. Untouched: a Claude seat has no home of its own, and OpenCode keeps sessions in the user's own storage.

watcher.$comment: Reads the turns of the roles in `watch` and tells the seat above when one goes off (Peer to Lead, Lead to Supervisor); it never stops, cancels or edits a seat. Code computes a turn's facts from its tool calls, and most turns end there at no cost; a rule stands on facts alone or asks a decision model one question about what the seat's message claims. mode: off does nothing; shadow scans into watch/scans.jsonl and mails nobody; on also mails. Shipped off; each machine chooses: install.sh asks once and writes the installed copy (`./install.sh --watcher off|shadow|on` changes it).
watcher.$comment_rules: raise: mail the seat above when mode is on; log: scan log only; off. The first thirteen stand on facts (tool calls, git, the brief); the last three ask the model. software-install: a tool or a browser put on the machine without the brief granting it; a project's own dependencies do not count. skill-skipped: a code-writing Peer reports CANDIDATE without candidate-handoff loaded, or edits under a law naming a skill it has not loaded; said once per skill and seat. It logs until a real room's count says the seat above should hear it. unverified-completion is not asked when checks ran but their result could not be read. external-action and reopen-condition log until this room's labels show they separate (seatwork_watch_stats).
watcher.$comment_thresholds: sleepSeconds: clock seconds a turn may wait in the shell (sleep, a sleeping loop) before it is told. repeatRun: the same action and result, back to back. cycleRepeats: rounds of a pattern of two to four actions. sameFailure: one check failing the same way. inFlightFactor: a running command may take this many times the role's stall minutes (room.params) before its silence is told.
watcher.$comment_scores: The score (0 to 1) from which a model-asking rule's finding counts; fitted to one model version and one revision of the questions (watch/questions.ts).
watcher.$comment_engine: The decision model. url: the full endpoint (TypeSafe's /v1/systemone and OpenRouter's /api/alpha/decisions take the same body). The key comes from the env var keyEnv, else the file keyFile under the room home; with none, the asking rules are logged as facts only. The endpoint gets the seat's last message and a few lines of its brief, never tool output.
watcher.$comment_budget: The model's cost, counted from the tokens each reply reports. Once a day has spent its share of the plan only end-of-turn questions are asked; at the cap, none until next month.
watcher.$comment_state: messageChars: a seat's final message goes to the model whole up to this; a longer one is cut to the lines a question reads, and a question whose lines do not fit is skipped that turn and named in the scan log. briefLineChars cuts each line of the brief.
watcher.$comment_calibration: How an asking rule earns `raise`. A turn is labelled by what the seat above did within labelWindowMinutes: ACCEPT, or REJECT / REVISED BRIEF (a HOLD is no verdict). Work returns for many reasons, so for unverified-completion a returned turn counts only if the seat above ran its own test before the verdict and saw it fail; else it is left out. A rule is fit with minLabels labelled turns separated at minAuroc or better, at a threshold flagging at most maxFalseRaiseRate of the accepted ones.

room.$comment: routes: who may mail whom; spawn: who may create whom. The plugin checks both, against mistakes: no security boundary, every seat runs as the same user. Nothing goes up from a Supervisor to hq (turn ends, permissions, GC notices, mail); hq looks at the room and sends down. role:spec in spawn allows that specialization only (supervisor: peer:research). Mail off the table or outside the tree is refused; a seat created outside spawn is archived and its parent told, though its first prompt may have started.
room.$comment_params: Quoted by role prompts as {{placeholders}}; change them here, never in a prompt. heartbeatCron: the Supervisor's beat; Lead reports that ask or close already wake it, so it only catches what slipped between. mailChars: the longest body seatwork_mail takes. peerStallMinutes: a Peer silent this long with nothing pending gets a status check; its turns take minutes. reviewStallMinutes: longer, for review, research and lens seats, which read long before writing. leadStallMinutes: a Lead silent this long with no running Peer or pending permission. readBudgetTokens: reading per Peer task before the Lead must split it; ~80k tokens (~320 KB of source) is what a default-tier model reasons over well. cheapReadBudgetTokens: the same for the cheap tier, which loses the thread sooner. rotateAtTokens: a Lead or Peer past this is named with its size to the seat above under its next report; each step rereads the whole context, so its next task goes to a fresh seat.
room.$comment_handin: freshEyes: a writing Peer's CANDIDATE returns to it once before its Owner reads it, for a pass over its own work as a reviewer would; the next one goes up, and each repair after a rejection owes the pass again. One short Peer turn, against a review round of two or three seats.
room.$comment_work: The work store in <project>/.seatwork/.work/ (work.db, with issues.jsonl as its text copy). busyTimeoutMs: a write waits this long on another process's, then fails as DATABASE_LOCKED. flushAfterMs: the text copy is written once per burst of writes, this long after the first. staleClaimMinutes: an issue in progress untouched this long shows in the graph's alerts. close.minReasonChars: a close says what was done and its commit or evidence. close.forbidSelfClose: an issue's holder cannot close it; its Owner does. A project's own .seatwork/.work/policy.json overrides any of these.
room.$comment_recovery: A failed turn, before anyone is told. A service error (anything but a quota, an account problem or a refused prompt) is retried after delaysSeconds, once per entry: the seat gets a short note and continues. A quota is waited out until the time its message names, else limitedMinutes at a time, limitedMaxHours at most; those waits use up no try. An account, a refused prompt, and a seat out of tries go to its Owner as FAILED.
